pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What are peers? (1 mark)
   A. Animals
   B. Only teachers
   C. Only parents
   D. People of your own age or class

2. What is a motion in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. A dance
   C. The statement the teams discuss
   D. A song

3. In the kite passage, what went wrong? (1 mark)
   A. The string broke
   B. The wind stopped
   C. The children fell
   D. The kite flew away forever

4. Which punctuation mark often follows an interjection showing strong feeling? (1 mark)
   A. Exclamation mark
   B. Full stop
   C. Colon
   D. Question mark

5. What is a stage direction? (1 mark)
   A. A price
   B. An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   C. The ending
   D. The title

6. What should you do after writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Never look at it
   B. Read it aloud with a partner
   C. Tear it
   D. Hide it

7. What is a call centre? (1 mark)
   A. A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   B. A market
   C. A farm
   D. A school

8. What should you do if you dialled a wrong number? (1 mark)
   A. Stay silent
   B. Shout at them
   C. Say sorry and end the call politely
   D. Call again angrily

9. Which describes an object by size and colour? (1 mark)
   A. A big red bag
   B. To bag
   C. A bag
   D. Bagging

10. What is news? (1 mark)
   A. Songs
   B. Information about recent events
   C. Riddles
   D. Old stories only

11. Which is a common field on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Type of soil
   B. Name
   C. Colour of the wall
   D. The number of windows

12. What does a signature show? (1 mark)
   A. Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   B. The paper size
   C. The price of a form
   D. The colour of a pen

13. What is a digital form? (1 mark)
   A. A form made of clay
   B. A form filled in on a device
   C. A paper airplane
   D. A form on a tree

14. What does a class monitor do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives
   B. Runs the school
   C. Cooks
   D. Helps lead the class

15. What is a talking object used for? (1 mark)
   A. To hide
   B. To play with
   C. To show who may speak
   D. To throw

16. What does answer when they call mean in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. A leader sleeps
   B. A leader responds when people need them
   C. A leader shouts
   D. A leader hides

17. What is a good leader described as in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. Fair and kind
   B. Angry
   C. Rude
   D. Lazy

18. Which two words in the poem Lead with honesty rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. fair and strong
   B. poem and song
   C. all and call
   D. leader and rule

19. Why do leaders need to give clear instructions? (1 mark)
   A. To make noise
   B. So people know exactly what to do
   C. To confuse people
   D. To waste time

20. What is the treasure hunt game used for? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Practising following instructions
   C. Learning to sing
   D. Drawing maps only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

22. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

23. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

24. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

25. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)

26. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

27. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

28. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

29. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — People of your own age or class
   Peers are people like you in age or class.

2. C — The statement the teams discuss
   The motion is the topic.

3. A — The string broke
   The string broke and the kite fell.

4. A — Exclamation mark
   Exclamation marks show strong feeling.

5. B — An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   Stage directions tell how to speak or move.

6. B — Read it aloud with a partner
   Reading aloud shows if it sounds natural.

7. A — A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   Call centre staff answer calls.

8. C — Say sorry and end the call politely
   Politeness matters.

9. A — A big red bag
   Big and red are adjectives.

10. B — Information about recent events
   News reports what has happened.

11. B — Name
   Name is a common field.

12. A — Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   A signature confirms you agree.

13. B — A form filled in on a device
   Digital forms are filled on phones or computers.

14. D — Helps lead the class
   A monitor helps the teacher lead.

15. C — To show who may speak
   Only the holder speaks.

16. B — A leader responds when people need them
   It means to respond to people's needs.

17. A — Fair and kind
   The poem advises fairness and kindness.

18. C — all and call
   All and call have the same ending sound.

19. B — So people know exactly what to do
   Clear instructions get work done safely.

20. B — Practising following instructions
   Each note gives the next instruction.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.
